tools.name: get_damage_rules
tools.description: The rules a host, platform or rental car company has to follow when charging a traveller for damage, for Australia or the US. Returns plain facts, the evidence to ask for, where to escalate and official sources. Use when someone asks whether a damage bill or charge is allowed or fair.

tools.name: check_deadlines
tools.description: Works out the dates that matter for a damage charge: whether an Airbnb host asked in time, when the traveller's reply window closes, and the US credit card dispute deadline. Only uses dates the user gives (YYYY-MM-DD).

tools.name: evidence_to_request
tools.description: The exact documents and photos a traveller should ask the host or rental company for before paying a damage charge.

tools.name: start_bill_check
tools.description: Returns a link that opens neatly's check on the website with the bill type and company already chosen, for when you can't pass the user's files yourself. If you can access the files, use check_bill instead.

tools.name: check_bill
tools.description: Runs neatly's free check on the user's actual damage bill. Send the bill (screenshot, photo or PDF) and/or the damage photos the host or rental company sent, as https links or base64. tools.description: Gets a neatly report by its link or id. Before the full report is unlocked: the verdict, stamps, the strongest point and how many more points there are. tools.name: list_companies
tools.description: Lists the hosts, platforms and rental car companies neatly checks bills from in Australia or the US, with a page about each and whether neatly has company-specific facts.

tools.name: check_fee
tools.description: Explains one type of damage-related fee and the law or platform rule that limits it, for Australia or a US state: loss of use, admin fee, processing fee, diminished value, repair estimate instead of an invoice, cleaning, wear and tear, old item charged as new, late damage request, deposit kept. tools.name: where_to_complain
tools.description: The escalation path for an unfair damage charge with official links: Australian state fair trading offices, the ACCC and AFCA, or in the US the card dispute route, state attorneys general, the FTC and CFPB, plus known company claim contacts.

tools.name: draft_evidence_request
tools.description: Writes a free, polite message asking the host or rental company for the evidence behind a damage charge, ready to paste. A general template: for a reply written around the user's actual bill and findings, run check_bill and the full report.

tools.name: list_guides
tools.description: Lists neatly's guides for Australia or the US: dispute letters, state fee laws, credit card cover, Airbnb responses, fair trading complaints and more. Each has a one-paragraph answer.

tools.name: get_guide
tools.description: Returns a whole neatly guide: the answer, every section, FAQs and sources. Use the slug from list_guides.

tools.name: about_neatly
tools.description: What neatly is, how the check works, the six agents, price, guarantee, privacy (photos are not kept), who runs it and the answers to common questions. Use it when the user asks whether neatly is trustworthy, what it costs or what happens to their photos.

tools.description: Same as get_report. Kept for older clients.
